audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer (FAV, 4/10) and the content layer disagreed about who wins the lane — the prose in whys/early/mid/late/spikes was written as though Sejuani wins it.
audit.why: 52.72% over 588 games, and the mirror page (sejuani__illaoi.json) rates the matchup HARD 7/10 from Sejuani's side and keeps that chart. The packet itself carries the defect 'level chart contradicts data: Illaoi wins 52.72% but the chart gives Sejuani 5/7 stages vs 0'. The win[] rows on disk already favour Illaoi, so the sides were left alone and the contradicting prose was rewritten to match them and the mirror.
audit.corrected: Chart sides kept (they agree with the mirror and the win rate); whys, early, mid, late and three spikes rewritten to stop claiming Sejuani wins.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0] called level 3-5 'your only even window' and spikes[2]/[3] gave the first-item and late windows to Sejuani.
audit.why: Illaoi's power curve here is the tentacle field, which grows for free, against a tank whose damage is flat. Harsh Lesson is 4s at 400 range; Sejuani's only gap-close or escape, Arctic Assault, is 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s at 650. A 4-second leap against an 18-second charge is not an 'even window', it is the lane.
audit.corrected: Level 3-5 restated as the best window with the real 4s vs 18s numbers; first-item and late spikes restated in Illaoi's favour.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page tracks 'Permafrost's cooldown' as the thing to fight around, and wants.foe[0] credits Permafrost with the slows.
audit.why: Riot's text: Permafrost (E) is 1.5s flat at 560 range and 'freezes and stuns an enemy champion that has maximum Frost stacks' — it does nothing without stacks and is never meaningfully on cooldown. The stacks and the slow both come from Winter's Wrath (W, 9/8/7/6/5s, 600 range, 'slowing enemies and applying Frost stacks'). Waiting for a 1.5-second cooldown is not a plan; waiting out the 9-second W is. Second missed interaction: Fury of the North grants 'immunity to slows' while Frost Armor is up, so the page's own Iceborn Gauntlet plan ('the slow makes tentacles land') does nothing until a Tentacle or auto strips the armor — Frost Armor only persists 'a short time after Sejuani takes damage'.
audit.corrected: Permafrost's 1.5s and its max-Frost precondition written in; Winter's Wrath (9s) named as the cooldown to count; Frost Armor's slow immunity stated against the Iceborn Gauntlet plan.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns named Permafrost as the matchup-defining cooldown with no number.
audit.why: Permafrost 1.5s, Winter's Wrath 9/8/7/6/5s, Arctic Assault 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s, Glacial Prison 120/105/90s. Against Illaoi's 16s Test of Spirit and 4s Harsh Lesson, the punishable cooldown is Arctic Assault: once she has charged in, she has no exit for up to 18 seconds.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into the cooldown block and report[5].

audit.why: 52.72% Emerald+ over 588 games; mirrors the 47.28% on the Sejuani page.

edits.before: Sejuani's Frost Armor and Permafrost slow tank your Level 1 and stick to you.
edits.after: Frost Armor breaks the moment a Tentacle lands, and she has no Level 1 answer to it.

edits.before: At Level 2 her sustain and chill keep you out of Tentacle range.
edits.after: At Level 2 her only escape, Arctic Assault, is still 18 seconds down.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay even as you contest slams against her Frost Armor.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are yours: her Winter's Wrath is 9s, your Harsh Lesson is 4s.

edits.before: Her first-item tankiness lets her stall out your E soul without dying.
edits.after: Your first item plus a Vessel's tentacles out-damage her flat tank scaling.

edits.before: Late, Sejuani's teamfight chill dictates fights and she declines your slam duel.
edits.after: Late she has to group, so catch her side-laning — one Vessel and the arms finish her.

edits.before: Your only even window: with W Harsh Lesson up you can W-gap and force a Tentacle slam before her Frost Armor passive resets, and landing E here is your best chance to punish her.
edits.after: Your best window: Harsh Lesson is a 4-second leap, so W in the moment Winter's Wrath is spent — her 18-second Arctic Assault is the only way out, and Permafrost cannot stun without stacks.

edits.before: Even itemized, her Permafrost slows and Frost Armor tankiness let her body-block your slams and stall until your E soul expires without dying.
edits.after: Iceborn Gauntlet's slow does nothing while Frost Armor holds — break the armor with a Tentacle first, then your slows land and the spirit dies.

edits.before: Sejuani is a scaling teamfight tank whose R and W chill dictate fights; she never has to duel you on your Tentacle field, so the raw lane stays against you.
edits.after: Sejuani scales as a teamfight tank, not a duellist — her damage stays flat while your field grows, so drag her side lane and make her fight on it.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are Sejuani's: her Frost Armor sustain and Permafrost slows let her tank your early Tentacle and stick to you while giving up nothing, so farm safe and don't chase.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are yours: Frost Armor gives resistances and slow immunity only out of combat, so the first Tentacle that connects strips it, and Arctic Assault is 18 seconds at rank 1.

edits.before: Levels 3-5 read as skill — with W online you can gap-close and force a Tentacle trade, and a well-timed E is your best punish, but her Frost Armor and slows make committing risky if her jungler is near.
edits.after: Levels 3-5 are firmly yours — Harsh Lesson is 4 seconds against an 18-second Arctic Assault, so walk her down, land Test of Spirit and slam. Only her jungler or a full Frost stack into Permafrost buys her the fight.

edits.before: From 6 on Sejuani takes over: R Glacial Prison hard-CCs you out of your own field, her chill dictates every fight, and she never has to duel you, so this stays a losing matchup on paper — win it with vision and side-lane pressure.
edits.after: From 6 you decide fights: Leap of Faith spawns an arm per champion hit, and Glacial Prison is her one 120-second answer. Respect the 1300-range bola, then take the side lane — she has to group, and a lone tank loses to a full field.

edits.before: Stack Permafrost slows to keep you out of Tentacle range
edits.after: Stack Frost with Winter's Wrath, then Permafrost-stun you

edits.before: Her stun after Frost stacks. Don't get stacked + stunned. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Permafrost is 1.5s — it stuns only at max Frost, so the cooldown to count is Winter's Wrath at 9s.

edits.before: - Sejuani Permafrost: matchup-defining — Her stun after Frost stacks. Don't get stacked + stunned. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Sejuani Permafrost (1.5s): it stuns only at max Frost — count Winter's Wrath (9s) and Arctic Assault (18s) instead. - Your Test of Spirit: 16s at rank 1 — never spend it on chip. - Leap of Faith: the win condition, kill windows only.

edits.before: Track Sejuani's Permafrost: Her stun after Frost stacks. Don't get stacked + stunned. When it is down — Land E, slam the spirit.
edits.after: Permafrost is 1.5s and stuns only at max Frost — count Winter's Wrath (9s). Frost Armor also blanks slows until you break it.

notes: The two layers told opposite stories on this page: the full layer said FAV 4/10 with Illaoi winning six of seven stages, while every content why[], the early/mid/late blocks and three of four spikes were written as though Sejuani wins the lane — even though win[0..3] on disk say Illaoi. The prose was brought to the sides, not the other way round, because the sides agree with the 52.72% win rate and with the already-audited mirror (sejuani__illaoi.json, HARD 7/10 from her side). Sejuani is female; the full layer refers to her as 'him' in tradeGood, ahead, breakdown.feeding, dontsFull[0].d and elsewhere — not fixed here because each is a one-word change inside otherwise correct prose, but it is worth a champion-level sweep. Illaoi kit-flag misfires again: R Leap of Faith carries 'grounding' and 'untargetable' flags and E Test of Spirit carries 'slow', none of which appear in Riot's descriptions — nothing written on them (the mirror agent flagged the same thing).
